reasons: gets paid between the grid and the chip
mentions.text:
Per Truist, AI data center capacity goes from 24 GW to 100 GW by 2030, and every one of those watts has to be converted, stored, smoothed and cooled before a single GPU turns on.

So I mapped every business that gets paid between the grid and the chip, seven layers from the grid to the GPU, and marked the one I'd watch most closely.

Infrastructure // getting megawatts into the building:
$ETN Eaton, $VRT Vertiv, $GEV GE Vernova, $SBGSY Schneider, $ABBNY ABB

Power supply // AC in, DC out:
Delta (https://t.co/tAcP8vyGJW), the cleanest pure play on the whole map Lite-On (https://t.co/RZNOwxTpNN), co-designed the GB300 power shelf $FLEX Flex, $AEIS Advanced Energy

DC-DC conversion // the last step before the silicon, and THE LAYER I'D WATCH:
$MPWR Monolithic Power, $VICR Vicor, $IFNNY Infineon, $TXN Texas Instruments, $ADI Analog Devices, $RNECY Renesas, $ON onsemi
As density rises, every point of efficiency here is worth more, and that's where pricing power can show up.

Battery backup // seconds to minutes when power drops:
$PCRFY Panasonic, Samsung SDI (006400.KS), LG Energy Solution (373220.KS) 

Capacitors // fractions of a second when GPU demand spikes:
Nippon Chemi-Con (6997.T), $MRAAY Murata, $TTDKY TDK, Yageo (https://t.co/yXXDTFGgaV), Samsung Electro-Mechanics (009150.KS)

Control // the nervous system:
$NXPI NXP, $STM STMicro, plus TI, ADI and Infineon again

Cooling // where every watt ends up:
$VRT Vertiv, Delta, $NJDCY Nidec

Panasonic shows up in six boxes on the map and Delta in four, and to me that's the tell, because the names that keep popping up are the ones getting paid more than once every time a rack gets built.

I broke down all seven layers in my latest article on Substack, including why they grow on three different demand curves and the five holes in the thesis, because I don't do one-sided. 

It's free to read, link in the comments.

Bullish ⚡️

reasons: Vera Rubin ramp pulling high-end capacitors
mentions.text:
$INTC $ARM $AMD $MU $SNDK

So now that pretty much every bottleneck has been discovered, from GPUs, CPUs and DRAM to NAND, HDDs, ABF substrates and MLCCs, what really matters is which one is the tightest.

TrendForce tracks seven parts of the AI server every week, and only one of them is balanced right now: the GPU. 

Everything that has to ship around it is tight or very tight, which means owning GPUs no longer guarantees you can build a server.

Here's the list ranked by how stretched lead times are versus a balanced market, with the timeline and the names for each:

ABF substrates // 48 to 56 weeks vs 12, about 4x normal. Bigger AI chips need more substrate layers, and while the glass fiber cloth shortage should ease gradually in 2027, yields on high-layer substrates keep supply tight beyond that. Ibiden (4062.T), Unimicron (https://t.co/AANrerOpo9), Kinsus (https://t.co/mWwb5BhOMJ), Nan Ya PCB (https://t.co/BQ6F6jvv9R), AT&S (https://t.co/tvexo6DkwA), and Nittobo (3110.T) for the glass cloth.

HDD // 50 weeks vs 16, about 3x. All that AI data has to live somewhere cheap, and vendors are adding capacity through HAMR, but the deficit is expected to last until at least 2027. $STX Seagate, $WDC Western Digital.

MLCC // 32 weeks vs 12, about 2.7x. The Vera Rubin ramp pulls high-end capacitors, and new capacity once planned for 4Q26 has slipped into 2027. $MRAAY Murata, Samsung Electro-Mechanics (009150.KS), Taiyo Yuden (6976.T), Yageo (https://t.co/yXXDTFGgaV), $TTDKY TDK.

DRAM // 20 weeks vs 8, about 2.5x. Talk of more price increases for 4Q26 into 1Q27 is building, especially for low-capacity modules. $MU Micron, $SKHY SK hynix, Samsung (005930.KS).

NAND / enterprise SSD // 16 weeks vs 8, 2x. Suppliers are shifting capacity toward enterprise SSDs for US cloud providers, and it still isn't enough. $SNDK SanDisk, Kioxia (285A.T), plus Samsung, SK hynix and Micron.

CPU // 25 to 30 weeks vs 16 to 20, about 1.5x, and new to the radar this week. Agentic AI is pulling server CPU demand while the big clouds speed up their own Arm-based chips. $AMD, $INTC, $ARM.

GPU // balanced at 30 to 40 weeks. Blackwell ships on schedule through 2026, and Rubin volumes scale from 2027. So now that pretty much every bottleneck has been discovered, from GPUs to memory to CPUs, what really matters is which one is the tightest.

The alpha now comes from spotting which part tightens next, and from knowing when relief is coming.

Bullish ⚡️
